title: Compression surgery lab log — week of 2028-03-27
content:
Field lab log for compression and quantization work — notes, quick results, and action items.

Meeting: Applied ML weekly research sync — Compression Surgery (Tue 2028-03-28, 11:00am PT)
Attendees: Maya C, Arjun P, Lina G, Theo P, guest: Sasha R (serving-runtime)
Purpose: Triage last week's 4-bit PTQ regressions, reconcile eval gaps, confirm KV-cache behavior, agree next experiments for onboarding 7B family into Dedicated.

Summary bullets:
- Short story: 4-bit PTQ on the 7B conversational checkpoint reduced memory by ~58% and reduced average serving cost estimate by ~47%, but introduced coherence regressions on long-context (>2048) instruction-following prompts.
- KV-cache hypothesis: regression correlates with KV cache sharding + quantized attention keys; when shard boundary aligns with model chunking we saw attention weight drift. Repro steps below.
- QAT quick-run: small QAT schedule (3 epochs, lr 2e-5) on 100k-dialog subset recovered ~70% of the lost instruction-follow scores while raising fine-tune cost; more targeted QAT on attention layer weights looks promising.

Experiments run this week (short notes):
1) ptq-4bit-symmetric-v1 (Arjun) — baseline PTQ using min-max symmetric per-tensor scaling.
   - dataset: 5k conv-turn prompts (diverse lengths 64-4096)
   - perf: peak GPU memory down 58%; throughput +11% on p4d (batch 1, seq 1024)
   - quality: Instr-Follow score -18% relative to fp16 on long prompts (>2048), negligible on short prompts.
   - notes: artifacts in PR #412; saved representative calibration set at s3://redwood-experiments/ptq/repcal-0328

2) ptq-4bit-perchannel-v2 (Lina) — per-channel symmetric scaling on query/key/value projections.
   - perf: marginally higher memory than per-tensor (~+3%); quality improved on some long-context cases but still 8-10% gap.
   - observation: per-channel helps head-wise variance but not cross-head coherence.

3) kv-shard-compatibility-check (Theo + Sasha) — created synthetic sequence that forces shard boundary mid-conversation.
   - reproduction: when shard size == 512 tokens, attention modulation at token 513 shows anomalous gradient of softmax magnitudes in quantized runs only.
   - fix candidate: preserve an fp32 shadow of attention keys across shard boundaries or apply overlap-copy of last 32 k-v tokens (cheap memory cost).

4) QAT-mini-sched (Maya) — 3-epoch QAT on 100k examples, only attention and ff modules, with distillation loss from fp16 baseline.
   - result: Instr-Follow recovered to -6% vs fp16; latency increased by ~4% at inference due to added shim layers.
   - tradeoff: QAT reduces immediate regressions but increases compute in training pipeline and adds complexity for model onboarding (we'd need QAT pipeline for every new checkpoint).

Evaluation notes and metrics (quick table summary):
- Dataset: 3 eval suites: conv-instr (2k), long-context stress (1k), instruction-follow holdout (1k).
- Key metrics: Instr-Follow score (0-100), Perplexity (lm), Avg token latency (ms), GPU memory (GB), Throughput tokens/s.
- Example numbers (ptq-4bit-perchannel-v2 vs fp16): Instr-Follow 84 vs 92, Perp 16.3 vs 14.1, latency 35ms vs 33ms (seq 1024), memory 9.8GB vs 23.4GB.

Open hypotheses and short tests to run next:
- H1: Localized QAT on attention-to-output projection only will yield >60% recovery without full QAT cost. (Runner: Maya, timeline: 1 week)
- H2: Small overlap-copy of last 32 KV tokens across shard boundaries will fix long-context drift with <2% memory overhead. (Runner: Theo + Sasha, timeline: 3 days)
- H3: Mixed-percentage quantization: keep query/key in 8-bit, others 4-bit. Evaluate latency/cost break-even. (Runner: Arjun, timeline: 5 days)

Decisions made in meeting:
- Stop blanket PTQ release for 7B until shard/kv behavior confirmed; allow internal canary only. (owner: Maya)
- Implement KV overlap experiment as highest priority; if it works, re-run full eval set. (owner: Theo)
- Begin small QAT prototype targeting only attention matrix multipliers; if it recovers >=70% of regression, schedule cost/benefit review for onboarding pipeline. (owner: Maya + Arjun)

Action items (explicit):
- Theo: implement KV 32-token overlap and push benchmark scripts to PR branch (due 2028-04-01). Linked: JIRA-ML-789.
- Arjun: run mixed-precision run (q/k=8bit others 4bit) on representative bench and post results (due 2028-04-03).
- Lina: aggregate failing prompts from long-context suite and produce a minimal reproducible set (target 50 prompts) for QAT distillation (due 2028-04-02).
- Maya: draft short doc (confluence) outlining tradeoffs for PTQ vs QAT for onboarding checklists (due 2028-04-06).

Notes to ops/serving team: Sasha — if KV overlap is necessary we'll need a small runtime change: a copy/concat at shard boundary and a toggle to disable for non-quantized models. Please review overhead estimate; Theo will ping you with microbench numbers.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: QAT pipeline increases onboarding latency for new checkpoints; mitigation: run QAT only for major releases and provide quantized fallback variants for minor patches.
- Risk: PTQ regressions may not show on short internal evals; mitigation: expand long-context suite and run randomized shard boundary stress tests in CI (low-cost nightly).

Notes & scraps (raw observations):
- Saw head 7's attention norm collapse in some reps — likely numeric underflow in min-max scaling. Try clipping extreme outliers pre-calibration.
- Example failing prompt saved: s3://redwood-experiments/ptq/failures/long-513-003.json (Lina)

Next sync: Tue 2028-04-04 11:00am PT, focus: KV overlap results, mixed-precision numbers, finalize small-QAT plan.


Appendix: quick command snippets used this week:
- run ptq baseline: python tools/ptq/run_ptq.py --model checkpoints/rw-7b/ep10 --calib s3://... --bits 4 --scheme symmetric --out artifacts/ptq/ptq-4bit-0328
- run eval: python eval/run_eval.py --model artifacts/ptq/ptq-4bit-0328 --suites long-context,conv-instr --out evals/0328/summary.json

Contact for clarifications: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai) — please add notes or push to the PR referenced above.
